_doc: Summary and topics for the DSA skill nodes (src/nexus/dsa-nodes.js), shown in each node's content view.

bit_basics.summary: You will be able to read problem statements carefully, handle fast input and output and implement straightforward simulations without bugs.
topics: Reading constraints and choosing data types
Simulating a process step by step

byte_sorting.summary: You will be able to sort data efficiently, write custom comparators and use counting sort when values are small.
topics: Built-in sort and O(n log n) bounds

byte_strings.summary: You will be able to manipulate strings, count characters, check palindromes and do simple pattern matching efficiently.

byte_brute.summary: You will be able to solve problems by complete search, enumerating candidates with recursion and backtracking and pruning the search.

kb_bsearch.summary: You will be able to apply binary search to sorted arrays and monotonic answers and solve range problems with two pointers.

kb_greedy.summary: You will be able to design greedy algorithms for scheduling and interval problems and justify them with exchange arguments.

kb_prefix.summary: You will be able to answer range sum queries in constant time with 1D and 2D prefix sums and apply range updates with difference arrays.
topics: Prefix sums with hash maps for subarray counts
Prefix XOR and other invertible operations

mb_ntheory.summary: You will be able to use primes, GCD, modular arithmetic and sieves to solve number theory problems within time limits.

mb_dp.summary: You will be able to define DP states and transitions and solve classic problems such as knapsack, LIS, LCS and coin change.
topics: Coin change counting and minimum coins

mb_graphs.summary: You will be able to represent graphs and use BFS and DFS to find components, shortest unweighted paths and bipartite structure.

mb_dsu.summary: You will be able to maintain dynamic connectivity with union-find using path compression, union by rank and weighted variants.

gb_adv_dp.summary: You will be able to solve harder DP problems over subsets, digits, trees and DAGs by choosing compact state representations.
topics: DP on trees with subtree states
DP on DAGs in topological order

gb_ds.summary: You will be able to choose and use stacks, queues, ordered sets, maps, priority queues and Fenwick trees to speed up solutions.

gb_trees.summary: You will be able to traverse trees, find diameters and lowest common ancestors and flatten trees with an Euler tour.

gb_spaths.summary: You will be able to compute shortest paths with Dijkstra, Bellman-Ford, Floyd-Warshall and 0-1 BFS and pick the right one.

tb_segtree.summary: You will be able to answer range queries with point and range updates using segment trees with lazy propagation and persistence.

tb_combo.summary: You will be able to count arrangements with permutations, binomial coefficients and inclusion-exclusion under a modulus.

tb_stralgo.summary: You will be able to match patterns in linear time with KMP and the Z-function and compare substrings fast with hashing.

pb_flows.summary: You will be able to model problems as network flows and solve max flow, min cut, bipartite matching and assignment problems.

pb_game.summary: You will be able to analyse impartial games with Sprague-Grundy theory and search game trees with minimax and alpha-beta pruning.
topics: Nim and XOR of pile sizes

pb_adv_trees.summary: You will be able to answer path and subtree queries with heavy-light and centroid decomposition and understand link-cut trees.

pb_geometry.summary: You will be able to solve computational geometry problems with cross products, convex hulls, segment intersection and polygon area.
topics: Polygon area with the shoelace formula

eb_fft.summary: You will be able to multiply polynomials and compute convolutions in O(n log n) with FFT and the number theoretic transform.

eb_dp_opt.summary: You will be able to speed up DP transitions with divide and conquer, Knuth's optimisation, convex hull trick and the aliens trick.

eb_adv_graphs.summary: You will be able to solve harder graph problems with SCCs, 2-SAT, block-cut trees and Euler paths.

zb_expert_ds.summary: You will be able to implement balanced and persistent structures such as treaps, splay trees and wavelet trees for advanced queries.
topics: Wavelet trees for k-th smallest queries

zb_expert_combo.summary: You will be able to count with generating functions, formal power series and Burnside's lemma and Polya enumeration.

yb_expert_trees.summary: You will be able to maintain dynamic forests with link-cut trees, Euler tour trees and top trees for path and subtree queries.

yb_expert_math.summary: You will be able to apply advanced mathematics such as elliptic curves, matroid intersection and multivariate polynomials in contest problems.

overflow_ascension.summary: You will combine techniques across every domain to solve elite contest problems that require several advanced ideas at once.
